one_line: First narcotics-related crypto SDN action: Chinese fentanyl kingpins Fujing Zheng, Guanghua Zheng and Xiaobing Yan designated under Kingpin Act with BTC/LTC addresses listed.
Farrukh Furkatovitch Fayzimatov designated for soliciting crypto donations for al-Qa'ida-affiliated Hayat Tahrir al-Sham network in Syria; crypto addresses listed.
First-ever sanction of a crypto mining company: BitRiver AG and ten Russian subsidiaries designated under EO 14024 for monetizing Russian energy via bitcoin mining (sanctions evasion).
Russian neo-Nazi paramilitary Task Force Rusich designated with 5 crypto addresses (2 BTC, 2 ETH, 1 USDT) used to crowdfund pro-Russian troops in Ukraine.
Genesis Market (credential/fraud shop) designated following Operation Cookie Monster takedown; crypto-payment cybercrime marketplace.
Wang Hongfei and Chinese chemical firms (WSBT, SXPC) designated for Bitcoin-based sale of fentanyl precursors; BTC address 3PKiHs4GY4rFg8dpppNVPXGPqMX6K2cBML listed.
Dubai-based John Desmond Hanafin and Huriya Private designated for crypto/financial-services facilitation of Russian sanctions evasion.
Chinyong IT Cooperation Co. and employee Kim Sang Man designated (with South Korea) for DPRK overseas IT-worker scheme; six crypto deposit addresses listed.
Large China-based fentanyl/synthetic-opioid producer network designated, including crypto addresses used to receive drug-payment proceeds.
DPRK hacking group Kimsuky and cyber actors designated for intelligence collection supporting the regime's nuclear/WMD program (crypto-linked cyber actor designation).
12 entities + 2 individuals incl. Russian virtual-currency exchanges Netex24 and Bitpapa designated for blockchain-based Russian sanctions evasion (links to Garantex/Hydra/Sberbank).
Hezbollah crypto financier Tawfiq Muhammad Sa'id al-Law designated for providing digital wallets/crypto transfers to Hezbollah and IRGC-QF; USDT (Tron) address listed.
Russian UAV developer OKO Design Bureau designated for soliciting crypto donations via Telegram to fund drone production for the war in Ukraine.
911 S5 residential-proxy botnet network designated: Yunhe Wang, Jingping Liu, Yanni Zheng + 3 entities, with 49 crypto addresses listed as identifiers for Wang.
Nordic Resistance Movement designated SDGT (with 3 leaders) for soliciting multi-asset crypto donations (BTC/ETH/LTC/USDT/XMR and others) to fund violent extremism.
Russian drone developer KB Vostok (Vostok Design Bureau) designated with crypto addresses used to solicit donations supporting UAV production for the war in Ukraine.
Tri-lateral (US/UK/AU) designation of Russia-based Evil Corp cybercrime syndicate (Dridex/BitPaymer) — additional members/facilitators incl. Eduard Benderskiy, crypto-laundering nexus.
Iran-based Nemesis darknet-market admin Behrouz Parsarad designated with 49 crypto addresses (44 BTC, 5 XMR) for facilitating fentanyl/cybercrime sales.
China-based Guangzhou Tengyue Chemical Co. and Huang Xiaojun designated for synthetic-opioid trafficking; crypto addresses used to receive payments.
Iranian financial facilitators Alireza Derakhshan and Arash Estaki Alivand designated for coordinating cryptocurrency transactions on behalf of the IRGC.
Prince Group TCO (Cambodia) and chairman Chen Zhi designated across 146 targets for pig-butchering crypto fraud / forced-labor scam compounds; ~$780M+ BTC attributed (parallel DOJ $15B seizure).
DPRK money-laundering network (Cheil/First Credit Bank, bankers Jang Kuk Chol & Ho Jong Son) designated; 53 crypto addresses (~$5.4M, much frozen by Tether) listed.
Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (Burma) + 4 leaders/companies designated for hosting Chinese-OC pig-butchering crypto scam compounds (Tai Chang near Myawaddy); part of Scam Center Strike Force.
Russian bulletproof-hosting provider Media Land LLC and Aleksandr Volosovik designated (tri-lateral) for enabling ransomware; associated network laundering stablecoins.

In the same March 21 2025 action that delisted the Tornado Cash entity/smart-contract addresses, OFAC removed co-founder Roman Semenov from the cyber-related (E.O. 13694) SDN designation while maintaining his separate North Korea/DPRK designation — a partial, individual-level removal distinct from the Tornado Cash entity delisting already in the corpus. NOTE: same OFAC Recent Action bundle (recent-actions/20250321) as existing corpus id tornado-cash-ofac-delisting-2025; include only if the corpus counts the Semenov cyber-removal as a separate designation-action.

actor: State of New York (Manhattan DA / NY State)
one_line: New York State indicted Arthur Budovsky and Vladimir Kats for running GoldAge Inc., an illegal money-transmitting digital-currency exchange, from their Brooklyn apartments; they were convicted/sentenced to five years probation in 2007 — the direct precursor to Liberty Reserve.

actor: US DOJ (Criminal Division Cybercrime/CEOS) + US Secret Service
one_line: Four-count indictment (handed down Apr 24, unsealed Apr 27, 2007) charging e-Gold Ltd, Gold & Silver Reserve, and principals Douglas Jackson, Reid Jackson and Barry Downey with money-laundering conspiracy and operating an unlicensed money-transmitting business; the seminal pre-Bitcoin digital-currency enforcement action (corpus has only the 2008 plea).

actor: US court order via the e-Gold indictment / US Secret Service
one_line: As a knock-on of the e-Gold indictment, a US court forced e-Gold to freeze/liquidate the e-gold accounts that backed 1MDC (an e-gold-backed digital gold currency), worth an estimated $10-20M, halting 1MDC redemptions and killing the platform by year-end 2007.

After James Fayed's arrest, the US Attorney unsealed an indictment of e-Bullion and Goldfinger Coin & Bullion for operating without a money-transmitter license under the USA PATRIOT Act; the e-Bullion.com site was taken down Aug 5, 2008 and assets (incl. the Perth-Mint bullion backing) were seized. (Corpus has a generic 2008-08 e-Bullion seizure entry; this captures the indictment-unsealing/site-takedown specifically.)

e-Gold principal Dr. Douglas Jackson sentenced to 300 hours community service, 3 years supervised release incl. 6 months home detention, plus fines; co-directors Reid Jackson and Barry Downey sentenced for unlicensed money transmitting — the sentencing phase distinct from the July 2008 guilty plea already in corpus.

actor: Supreme Court of Iceland (re Valitor / Visa Iceland)
one_line: Iceland's Supreme Court upheld the district court and ruled Valitor's 2011 closure of the WikiLeaks/DataCell donation gateway illegal, ordering it reopened within two weeks or face daily fines; Valitor reopened then cancelled the contract — the appellate capstone to the DataCell case (corpus has only the 2012-07 district-court ruling).

actor: US Treasury/FinCEN (PATRIOT Act Sec. 311) + US DOJ (SDNY) + HSI/USSS + 17-country action
one_line: Coordinated global takedown of Liberty Reserve: FinCEN named it a primary money-laundering concern (first Section 311 use against a virtual-currency provider), SDNY unsealed a 7-defendant indictment alleging $6B laundered, Budovsky and others were arrested across 17 countries, Costa Rica raided offices, and the liberty reserve domains were seized. (Corpus has only the 2011 Costa Rica license denial.)

actor: US Bankruptcy Court, Northern District of Texas (Dallas) / Mt. Gox foreign representative
one_line: US Bankruptcy Court in Dallas granted Chapter 15 recognition of Mt. Gox's Japanese insolvency (filed Mar 9, 2014), staying US class-action seizure of Mt. Gox US assets/servers — a distinct US legal action separate from the Tokyo bankruptcy already in corpus.

CFPB issued a consumer advisory (Aug 11, 2014) warning that virtual currencies are volatile, hacking-prone, uninsured and lack recourse, and began accepting consumer complaints against virtual-currency companies — the first US federal consumer-protection action targeting crypto.

Liberty Reserve founder Arthur Budovsky sentenced in Manhattan federal court to 20 years imprisonment and a $500,000 fine after pleading guilty (Jan 2016) to money-laundering conspiracy; admitted laundering $250M-$550M — the capstone of the Liberty Reserve enforcement timeline.

SEC Section 21(a) Report of Investigation on The DAO concluded that DAO tokens were securities, establishing the registration-or-enforcement mandate that drives subsequent US geofencing and token delisting across exchanges and platforms.

actor: DOJ (USAO-SDNY) / Sohrab Sharma, Robert Farkas, Raymond Trapani
one_line: DOJ criminally charged Centra Tech co-founders over a fraudulent $25M+ ICO (CTR tokens) with fabricated Visa/Mastercard partnerships and fake executives; Sharma sentenced to 8 years and ~$36M forfeiture.

LocalBitcoins OTC trader 'Bitcoin Maven' sentenced for operating an unlicensed money transmitting business and laundering purported drug proceeds ($6-9.5M in trades); forfeited 40 BTC, $292K cash, and gold bars; representative early P2P-exchanger MSB prosecution.

SEC settled with TokenLot LLC (an 'ICO superstore' secondary token trading platform) for unregistered broker-dealer activity, forcing the platform to wind down; first SEC broker-dealer registration action against a token trading venue.

SEC settled charges against EtherDelta founder Zachary Coburn for operating an unregistered national securities exchange (a DEX smart-contract order book), the first SEC action treating a decentralized exchange as an illegal unregistered exchange.

actor: DOJ (USAO-SDNY) / Ruja Ignatova, Konstantin Ignatov, Mark Scott
one_line: DOJ charged leaders of OneCoin, a >$4B fraudulent cryptocurrency scheme; Ignatova ('Cryptoqueen') indicted and on FBI Ten Most Wanted; brother Konstantin Ignatov and lawyer Mark Scott convicted/sentenced for fraud and laundering $400M.

FinCEN assessed its first-ever civil penalty against an individual peer-to-peer convertible-virtual-currency exchanger (Eric Powers, $35,350) for BSA registration, AML program, and reporting violations.

DOJ charged Reginald Fowler (Crypto Capital 'shadow banker' for Bitfinex/Binance and other exchanges) with bank fraud and operating an unlicensed money transmitting business; processed >$750M for VASPs; pleaded guilty, sentenced to ~6 years.

DOJ announced its then-largest-ever terrorism crypto seizure: 300+ cryptocurrency accounts, websites and pages tied to al-Qaeda, ISIS and Hamas's al-Qassam Brigades crypto donation campaigns (incl. ISIS PPE scam by Murat Cakar).

SEC obtained final judgment against Kik Interactive for the unregistered $100M Kin token offering; court found Kin sales were unregistered securities and Kik paid a $5M penalty (corpus has Telegram/TON but not Kik).

SEC charged LBRY with unregistered sale of LBC tokens; the Nov 2022 court ruling that LBC was a security (even outside an ICO, for consumptive use) led LBRY to cease operations and shut down the platform.

DOJ seized ~63.7 BTC (~$2.3M) representing the bulk of the Colonial Pipeline ransom paid to the DarkSide ransomware group, by obtaining the private key to a tracked address; landmark ransomware crypto clawback.
SEC settled $10.4M charges against Poloniex for operating an unregistered digital asset exchange, contributing to the platform's exit from the US market and delisting of tokens deemed securities.

DOJ charged two REvil ransomware actors and seized ~39.9 BTC plus $6.1M in ransom proceeds; Vasinskyi extradited (Mar 2022), sentenced (2024) to ~13.6 years and $16M restitution for the Kaseya attack.

DOJ arrested married couple and seized ~94,000 BTC (~$3.6B, then-largest financial seizure in DOJ history) tied to laundering proceeds of the 2016 Bitfinex exchange hack; guilty pleas Aug 2023, sentenced Nov 2024 (Lichtenstein 5 yrs, Morgan 18 mo).

Federal grand jury indicted BitConnect founder Satish Kumbhani for a global $2.4B cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme (BitConnect Lending Program); charges include wire fraud, commodity price manipulation, unlicensed money transmission; defendant a fugitive.

NetWalker ransomware affiliate Sebastien Vachon-Desjardins extradited from Canada and pleaded guilty (Jun 2022) to US computer/wire fraud and extortion charges; agreed to forfeit ~$21.5M plus BTC; sentenced to 20 years.

CFTC imposed a $250K penalty on bZeroX LLC and its founders (Tom Bean, Kyle Kistner) for the bZx leveraged-trading protocol and ordered cessation; distinct from the Ooki DAO successor suit already in the corpus.

DOJ announced guilty plea and historic seizure of ~50,676 BTC (~$3.36B) that James Zhong fraudulently obtained from Silk Road in 2012; second-largest financial seizure in DOJ history; distinct from 2013 Silk Road takedown.

actor: DOJ (W.D. Wash.) / Sergei Potapenko & Ivan Turogin (HashFlare/Polybius)
one_line: DOJ indicted HashFlare co-founders over a >$550M crypto-mining fraud (equipment performed <1% of claimed hashpower) plus the Polybius ICO; extradited from Estonia 2024; pleaded guilty Feb 2025.

actor: DOJ (USAO-SDNY) / David Carmona et al. (IcomTech), da Silva/Tacuri et al. (Forcount)
one_line: DOJ charged founders/promoters of two crypto Ponzi schemes, IcomTech and Forcount, promising guaranteed returns from purported mining/trading; IcomTech founder Carmona later sentenced to 121 months.

DOJ charged Avraham Eisenberg over the ~$110M Mango Markets DeFi oracle-manipulation exploit; convicted Apr 2024 (commodities fraud/manipulation, wire fraud); convictions later overturned May 2025 on venue/fraud-standard grounds.
SEC and 53 jurisdictions settled $45M with Nexo over its Earn Interest Product; Nexo agreed to cease offering the crypto lending product to US investors, exiting the US retail market.

actor: DOJ (USAO-DC) / Sim Hyon Sop (North Korean FTB rep)
one_line: DOJ criminal indictment of North Korean Foreign Trade Bank representative Sim Hyon Sop for two crypto laundering conspiracies (with OTC traders and with DPRK IT workers placed at US crypto firms); the criminal charge, distinct from the same-day OFAC SDN designation.

CFTC issued simultaneous settlement orders against DeFi protocol operators Opyn, ZeroEx (0x), and Deridex for illegal leveraged digital-asset derivatives, sending a 'register or geoblock US users / leave the US market' message that drove DeFi frontends to geofence Americans.

FinCEN issued a Section 311 NPRM designating international convertible virtual currency mixing as a class of transactions of primary money laundering concern (first activity-based, not entity/jurisdiction-based, special measure); mandate-listed 'Bitcoin mixer NPRM 2023'.

actor: DOJ (USAO-EDNY) / Braden John Karony, Kyle Nagy, Thomas Smith
one_line: DOJ unsealed indictment against SafeMoon executives for securities fraud, wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy over a rug-pull; falsely claimed liquidity was 'locked'; CEO Karony convicted May 2025, sentenced to 100 months and $7.5M forfeiture.

Darknet drug vendor Banmeet Singh (Silk Road, AlphaBay, Hansa, etc.) pleaded guilty and forfeited ~$150M in Bitcoin (~8,100 BTC), one of the largest DOJ crypto forfeitures from a darknet narcotics enterprise; sentenced to 8 years.

actor: DOJ / Xue Samuel Lee, Brenda Chunga, Rodney Burton (HyperFund)
one_line: DOJ brought criminal charges against the founder and top promoters of HyperFund (HyperVerse/HyperTech), a ~$1.7B global crypto Ponzi/pyramid scheme falsely claiming bitcoin-mining revenue; parallel SEC action.
SEC and state regulators ($3M total) charged TradeStation Crypto over an unregistered interest-bearing crypto lending product; TradeStation discontinued its US crypto services by Feb 22, 2024.

SEC charged ShapeShift AG ($275K cease-and-desist) for operating ShapeShift.io as an unregistered dealer in crypto-asset securities; mandate-listed action over the platform that had already exited US custodial exchange operations.

Operator of Bitcoin Fog darknet cryptocurrency mixer convicted (Mar 2024) of money laundering conspiracy and unlicensed money transmission; ~1.2M BTC (~$400M) laundered; sentenced Nov 2024 to 150 months; ~1,354 BTC plus Kraken account crypto forfeited.

BTC-e operator Alexander Vinnik pleaded guilty to money laundering conspiracy (exchange processed >$9B, ~1M users, laundered Mt. Gox-stolen BTC); distinct disposition from the 2017 indictment; case dismissed Feb 2025 via US-Russia prisoner swap.

SEC sued Consensys alleging MetaMask Swaps and Staking made it an unregistered broker and underwriter of Lido/Rocket Pool liquid-staking securities; mandate-listed suit targeting the dominant Ethereum wallet frontend (dismissed 2025).
SEC settled with Plutus Lending (dba Abra) over the unregistered Abra Earn crypto lending product (~$500M from US investors), forcing the product's wind-down and US market exit ($1.65M penalty).

SEC settled with eToro USA ($1.5M); eToro agreed to cease trading in nearly all crypto assets for US customers, restricting them to only BTC, ETH, and BCH and liquidating other holdings after a 180-day window.

actor: DOJ (E.D. Va.) / Sergey Ivanov & Timur Shakhmametov (Cryptex, UAPS, PM2BTC, Joker's Stash)
one_line: DOJ charged two Russian nationals for operating billion-dollar money-laundering/no-KYC crypto exchange services (Cryptex, UAPS, PM2BTC) and the Joker's Stash carding site; Secret Service/Dutch police seized domains and >$7M; parallel OFAC action.

DOJ indicted three operators of crypto mixers Blender.io and Sinbad.io for money laundering and unlicensed money transmission; two arrested Dec 2024; services used to launder ransomware and theft proceeds (incl. DPRK Lazarus).

actor: DOJ (USAO-SDNY) / OKX (Aux Cayes Fintech Co. Ltd.)
one_line: OKX operator Aux Cayes Fintech pleaded guilty to operating an unlicensed money transmitting business and agreed to pay >$504M; admitted >$1T in unregistered US transactions and facilitating >$5B in suspicious transfers (2018-2024).

actor: DOJ (E.D. Va.) / Aleksej Besciokov & Aleksandr Mira Serda (Garantex)
one_line: DOJ unsealed indictment of Garantex co-founders for money laundering conspiracy, sanctions evasion (IEEPA) and unlicensed money transmission; Secret Service seized Garantex domains and froze >$26M; Besciokov arrested in India Mar 2025.

DOJ filed civil forfeiture complaint against over $7.74M in crypto laundered by North Korean IT workers (using fake identities at US crypto firms) for the DPRK government, funds restrained in connection with the 2023 Sim indictment.

DOJ filed a civil forfeiture action against ~$225M in USDT, the largest scam-related crypto seizure in US history, tracing pig-butchering investment-fraud proceeds (linked to a Philippines scam compound and a Kansas bank collapse).

FinCEN assessed a $3.5M civil penalty against former P2P crypto exchange Paxful for willful BSA violations (failure to register as MSB, no AML program, no SARs, enabling Iran/DPRK-linked transactions); paired with a DOJ guilty plea.

actor: Costa Rica SUGEF (Superintendencia General de Entidades Financieras)
one_line: Costa Rica's financial regulator SUGEF denied Liberty Reserve's money-transmitting license application in 2009, finding it lacked basic AML/KYC controls — the earliest regulatory action against Liberty Reserve, predating the 2011 closure already in corpus. (Possible partial overlap with corpus 2011 entry; flagged for adjudication.)

actor: US Senators Charles Schumer & Joe Manchin (letter to DEA/DOJ)
one_line: Senators Schumer and Manchin sent a letter to the DEA and DOJ demanding federal action to shut down the Silk Road marketplace and naming Bitcoin as an 'untraceable' money-laundering currency — the first high-level US political pressure to target a crypto-payment network, a precursor to the 2013 Silk Road seizure.

actor: Ukraine Ministry of Revenues and Duties (tax police) + National Bank of Ukraine
one_line: Ukrainian tax police raided WebMoney's Ukrainian guarantor, seized computer equipment and froze ~UAH 60M (~$7.5M), blocking all Ukrainian WebMoney transactions; the NBU declared WebMoney unlicensed and an 'illegal system' suspected of laundering/tax evasion (funds unfrozen Mar 2014).

Banque de France published a 6-page note 'Les dangers liés au développement des monnaies virtuelles: l'exemple du bitcoin' (Dec 5, 2013) stating Bitcoin is neither legal-tender currency nor a means of payment under the Monetary and Financial Code, warning of the risks.

Norway's Director General of Taxation ruled (Dec 2013) that Bitcoin does not qualify as money/currency and will be treated as a taxable capital asset subject to capital-gains and (for business) VAT/wealth tax, an early state non-recognition stance.

actor: Banque du Liban (Central Bank of Lebanon)
one_line: Banque du Liban issued a public warning in Dec 2013 against the use of Bitcoin and other unregulated digital currencies, the first Middle East central bank stance, citing money-laundering, fraud and lack of legal backing.

RBI issued its first public caution (press release Dec 24, 2013) warning holders/traders of virtual currencies of legal/financial/security risks and stating it had not authorised any entity to deal in Bitcoin or any virtual currency.
Bank Negara Malaysia statement (Jan 3, 2014) stated Bitcoin is not recognised as legal tender in Malaysia and is not regulated by the central bank, cautioning the public on the risks.
Taiwan's FSC blocked Robocoin Bitcoin ATM installations and barred banks/financial institutions from converting or using Bitcoin as a payment tool via ATMs, ruling Bitcoin is not a currency.

actor: National Bank of Belgium (NBB) and FSMA
one_line: NBB and FSMA issued a joint press release (Jan 2014) warning consumers that virtual currencies are not legal tender, are unregulated, and carry significant risks.

actor: Prosecutor General's Office of the Russian Federation
one_line: Russia's Prosecutor General's Office declared on Feb 6, 2014 that anonymous payment systems and cyber-currencies including Bitcoin are illegal 'monetary surrogates' that cannot be used by individuals or legal entities, the country's first official prohibition stance (distinct from the Jan 2014 CBR letter already in corpus).
Central Bank of Jordan (2014) prohibited banks, financial companies and payment-service providers from dealing in Bitcoin or other virtual currencies and warned the public of associated risks.
Central Bank of Jordan circular prohibited banks, exchanges, and payment companies from dealing in bitcoin/cryptocurrencies, a standing ban maintained until a 2025 regulatory pivot.

State Bank of Vietnam press release (Feb 27, 2014) declared Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies are not legal means of payment and warned institutions/individuals against issuing, supplying or using them.
Banxico issued a statement (March 2014) warning that virtual assets such as Bitcoin are not legal tender in Mexico, are not issued or backed by the central bank, and carry significant risks.

Denmark's central bank stated (March 2014) Bitcoin is not a real currency ('more similar to glass beads') and the Danish FSA confirmed it falls outside its regulatory remit and is not legal tender, an early Nordic non-recognition stance.

actor: People's Bank of China (PBOC) / Chinese commercial banks (ABC, ICBC, etc.)
one_line: Around an April 15, 2014 deadline attributed to PBOC, major Chinese banks (Agricultural Bank of China and others) closed the accounts of bitcoin exchanges including OKCoin, Huobi and BTC Trade, cutting fiat on/off-ramps (the operational follow-through to the Dec 2013 PBOC notice already in corpus).

National Bank of Cambodia stated in 2014 it would not recognise Bitcoin (no central-bank issuer/backing) as legal tender or a monetary instrument and warned of risks including links to illicit activity.

Ecuador's National Assembly amended its monetary/financial code in July 2014 to ban decentralized digital currencies (Bitcoin) while authorizing a state-run electronic money system, with power to confiscate holdings and prosecute users of prohibited digital currencies.

actor: National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic (NBKR)
one_line: NBKR statement (Aug 2014) declared using Bitcoin and other virtual currencies as a means of payment illegal because the som is the sole legal tender in Kyrgyzstan.

Russia's Finance Ministry published a draft bill (Aug 2014 announced, fines schedule released Oct 3, 2014) to amend the Central Bank law to explicitly ban monetary surrogates including cryptocurrencies, with proposed fines up to 1M rubles for legal entities.

Central Bank of Kenya public notice cautioning against virtual currencies (Bitcoin), declaring them not legal tender; followed by a standing circular barring regulated banks from dealing with crypto firms.
CBK public notice cautioning against virtual currencies, then a standing circular barring banks from servicing crypto firms.
Central Bank of Iraq prohibited the use of cryptocurrencies by banks and currency traders in 2017, a standing ban citing AML/financial-stability risk.
Central Bank of Iraq prohibited use of cryptocurrencies by banks and currency traders in 2017.
NRB banned Bitcoin transactions under the Foreign Exchange (Regulation) Act 1962 on Aug 13 2017, leading to CIB arrests of seven exchange operators in Oct 2017.

SBV declared Bitcoin and similar virtual currencies not lawful means of payment (Official Letter 5747/NHNN-PC, Jul 2017) and that issuance/supply/use of them as payment is illegal and punishable by fines up to VND 200m from Jan 1 2018; reinforced by PM Directive 10/CT-TTg (Apr 2018).

actor: Morocco Office des Changes, Bank Al-Maghrib, Ministry of Economy and Finance
one_line: Morocco's foreign-exchange authority and central bank issued a joint statement declaring cryptocurrency transactions illegal under FX rules, with penalties, citing fraud/ML/TF risk.

Bangladesh Bank reaffirmed (2017 warning, and via CID letters) that transacting in and promoting cryptocurrencies is illegal under FX and AML laws, the 2022 FX regulations re-affirming virtual currencies 'are not permitted'; CID/BFIU enforcement led to arrests (e.g., 14 in Dhaka, Jul 2022). Distinct from the 2014 BB warning in corpus.

Bangladesh Bank reaffirmed (2017 warning and via CID letters) that transacting in and promoting cryptocurrencies is illegal under FX and AML laws, with the 2022 FX regulations re-affirming virtual currencies 'are not permitted'; CID/BFIU enforcement led to arrests (e.g., 14 in Dhaka, Jul 2022). Distinct from the 2014 BB warning in corpus.
Algeria's 2018 Finance Law prohibited the purchase, sale, use, and possession of virtual currency (later hardened by Law 25-10).
Algeria Finance Law 2018 prohibited the purchase, sale, use and possession of virtual currency.
A 2018 Central Bank of Tunisia directive criminalized most crypto activity absent state authorization, with fines and up to five years' imprisonment.
A 2018 Central Bank of Tunisia directive criminalized most crypto activity absent state authorization.

Bank Indonesia formally declared cryptocurrencies not a legitimate payment instrument under Currency Law 7/2011 and barred payment firms (PJSP/fintech) from processing virtual-currency transactions (per PBI 18/40/2016 and 19/12/2017).
Bank Indonesia declared crypto not a legitimate payment instrument and barred payment firms from processing crypto.

Real-name verified bank-account system took effect Jan 30 2018: anonymous virtual accounts for crypto trading banned; deposits allowed only where the exchange-account name matches a real-name bank account at the same bank, with minors and foreigners barred.

SBP BPRD Circular No. 03 of 2018 barred all banks, DFIs, microfinance banks and payment-system operators from processing, trading, holding or facilitating any virtual-currency/ICO-token transactions, declaring crypto not legal tender.

State Bank of Pakistan Circular No. 3 of 2018 advised banks/financial institutions not to process, use, trade, or facilitate virtual-currency transactions, effectively banning crypto banking rails (later cited under FATF grey-list pressure).
SBP Circular No.3 of 2018 barred banks from processing or facilitating virtual-currency transactions.

actor: National Bank of Cambodia + SECC + National Police
one_line: NBC, the securities regulator (SECC) and the General-Commissariat of National Police issued a joint statement (May 11 2018) prohibiting the propagation, circulation, buying, selling, trading and settlement of cryptocurrencies without a license — a de facto ban since no licenses were granted.
RBZ Circular No. 2/2018 ordered all banks to stop servicing crypto exchanges (naming Golix/Bitfinance and Styx24) within 60 days; Golix obtained a High Court provisional suspension on 24 May 2018.
RBZ Circular 2/2018 ordered banks to stop servicing crypto exchanges Golix and Styx24 within 60 days; later court-suspended.

actor: Saudi Standing Committee on unauthorized securities (CMA, SAMA, MoI, MoCI, MoMedia)
one_line: Saudi inter-agency Standing Committee declared trading in unauthorized virtual currencies (incl. Bitcoin) illegal in the Kingdom, warning against promotion and dealing.
NYDFS denied Bittrex's BitLicense application (AML/capital deficiencies) and ordered it to wind down/transfer NY-resident positions by 9 June 2019, forcing a NY exit.
NYDFS denied Bittrex BitLicense and ordered NY wind-down by June 2019.

actor: People's Bank of China + Shenzhen authorities
one_line: 2019 reaffirmation crackdown: PBOC moved to block access to domestic and offshore crypto-exchange and ICO websites via the Great Firewall, and in November 2019 Shenzhen authorities identified 39 exchanges violating the trading ban and initiated corrective action.

Pre-law FATF-Travel-Rule-driven delistings: Upbit ceased trading of six privacy coins (Monero, Dash, Zcash, Haven, BitTube, PIVX) on Sept 30 2019 and OKEx Korea delisted five (incl. Monero, Zcash, Dash) effective Oct 10 2019 citing inability to collect travel-rule data.

Supreme Court (IAMAI v RBI) quashed the April 2018 RBI banking ban on crypto as a disproportionate Article 19(1)(g) restriction, restoring banks' ability to service crypto businesses — the judicial reversal of the corpus's india-rbi-crypto-ban-2018.

Revised Financial Instruments and Exchange Act / Payment Services Act (effective May 1 2020) capped crypto margin-trading leverage at 2x and required exchanges offering margin/derivatives to register, tightening the prior self-imposed 4x cap.

CBM Directive 9/2020 (May 15 2020) made buying, selling, trading or transferring any cryptocurrency illegal under the Central Bank Law, AML Law and Financial Institutions Law, with account closures and criminal penalties; reaffirmed May 2024.

Egypt's Central Bank and Banking Sector Law No. 194 of 2020 prohibited issuing, trading, or promoting cryptocurrencies without a CBE license (preceded by the CBE's Jan 2018 warning and Dar al-Ifta haram fatwa).
Egypt Banking Law 194/2020 prohibited issuing, trading or promoting crypto without a CBE license.

SCA Decision No. 23/RM of 2020 (Crypto Asset Activities Regulation) imposed a federal onshore licensing regime over crypto offering, exchange, custody, and related services in the UAE outside the financial free zones.
SCA Decision 23 of 2020 imposed a federal onshore licensing regime over crypto offering, exchange and custody.

actor: Qatar Central Bank (Circular 6/2018) + Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority
one_line: Qatar banned crypto services: QCB Circular No. 6 of 2018 barred financial institutions from crypto dealing, and the QFCRA prohibited all virtual asset services within/from the QFC (formalized Dec 26, 2020), excepting token securities.
QCB Circular 6/2018 barred banks from crypto; QFCRA prohibited virtual-asset services in the QFC in Dec 2020.

Amended Special Financial Transactions Act enforcement decree (effective Mar 25 2021) effectively barred exchanges from handling 'dark coins' (Monero, Zcash, Dash, etc.), prohibiting domestic circulation of privacy coins on AML grounds.

CBSL public notice (Apr 9 2021) stated crypto is not legal tender, no ICOs/mining/exchanges are authorized, and a Foreign Exchange Act directive prohibited bank and card payments for crypto transactions; warning reiterated amid the 2022 economic crisis.

CBSL public notice (Apr 9 2021) stated crypto is not legal tender, no ICOs/mining/exchanges are authorized, and a Foreign Exchange Act directive prohibited bank and card payments for crypto transactions; warning reiterated amid the 2022 economic crisis.

Chinese search engines and social platforms (Baidu, Weibo, Sogou, Zhihu) began censoring keyword searches and accounts for Binance, OKEx and Huobi, returning legal-compliance error messages — June 2021 search/social censorship wave distinct from the March 2021 Weibo account purge already in corpus.
Thai SEC banned licensed exchanges from listing/trading meme tokens, fan tokens, NFTs, and exchange-issued tokens, ordering delisting within ~30 days.
Thai SEC banned exchanges from listing meme tokens, fan tokens, NFTs and exchange tokens, with 30-day delisting.

PBOC summoned ICBC, AgBank, China Construction Bank, Postal Savings Bank, Industrial Bank and Alipay, ordering them to identify crypto-linked accounts and cut off payment channels for virtual-currency trading — fiat-rail de-risking distinct from the September 2021 comprehensive ban.

Taiwan brought VASPs under the Money Laundering Control Act effective Jul 1 2021, then via the July 2024 AML Act amendment imposed mandatory FSC AML registration before operating with criminal penalties (up to 2 years / NT$5m) for unregistered operation.

actor: US state securities regulators (NJ, TX, AL, KY, VT)
one_line: Several US states (New Jersey first, then Texas, Alabama, Kentucky, Vermont) issued cease-and-desist orders against BlockFi Interest Accounts as unregistered securities, presaging the $100M federal/state settlement.

actor: US states NJ TX AL KY VT
one_line: Several US states issued cease-and-desist orders against BlockFi Interest Accounts as unregistered securities.

NRB issued a notice on Sept 9 2021 declaring the use, trading and mining of any form of cryptocurrency illegal, escalating the 2017 payment ban into a comprehensive prohibition with criminal penalties.

actor: Nepal Rastra Bank / Government of Nepal
one_line: Nepal banned bitcoin transactions in Aug 2017 (with arrests of exchange operators) and expanded the prohibition to use, trading, and mining of all cryptocurrency via a Sept 2021 government/NRB notice.
Nepal banned bitcoin in 2017 with arrests and expanded to use, trading and mining of all crypto via a Sept 2021 notice.

actor: US state securities regulators (NJ, TX, AL, KY)
one_line: Multiple US states (New Jersey, Texas, Alabama, Kentucky) issued cease-and-desist actions against Celsius's Earn Rewards interest accounts as unregistered securities.

actor: US states NJ TX AL KY
one_line: Multiple US states issued cease-and-desist actions against Celsius Earn Rewards accounts as unregistered securities.

NDRC and nine other authorities jointly issued the Notice on Regulating Virtual Currency Mining Activities, classifying crypto mining as an industry to be eliminated under the Industrial Structure Adjustment Catalogue and cutting electricity/financial support; distinct from the May 2021 State Council mining crackdown and the same-day PBOC trading ban.

Sept 24 2021 registration deadline under the amended Specific Financial Information Act: exchanges needed ISMS certification plus real-name bank-account contracts; ~36 of ~60 exchanges shut down, only 5 (Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Korbit, later Gopax) retained KRW fiat services.

MUI's 7th Ijtima Ulama fatwa (Nov 9-11 2021) declared cryptocurrency haram both as currency and as a tradable commodity/asset citing gharar, dharar and qimar; East Java NU issued a parallel haram ruling — non-binding but adoption-suppressing religious authority.

MAS Guidelines on Provision of DPT Services to the Public (Jan 17 2022) barred crypto service providers from marketing/advertising to the general public — no ads on public transport, websites, social media, broadcast/print media, physical ATMs, or via influencers; promotion limited to own channels.

Finance Act 2022 introduced a flat 30% tax on virtual-digital-asset income (s.115BBH, no loss offset/carry-forward) and a 1% TDS on transfers (s.194S, effective Jul 1 2022) — punitive fiscal regime that collapsed domestic exchange volumes.

Tencent's WeChat suspended 10+ public accounts tied to NFT/digital-collectible trading (Mar 2022), updated terms to ban crypto/NFT discussion (Jun 2022), then shut its own Huanhe NFT platform (Jul 2022) under government policy — platform-level account takedowns distinct from the June 2022 industry self-discipline pact in corpus.
Thai SEC/BOT prohibited the use of digital assets as a means of payment for goods and services effective April 1 2022, barring crypto-payment services by licensed operators.

India's Finance Act 2022 imposed a flat 30% tax on virtual-digital-asset gains (no loss set-off, from 1 Apr 2022) and a 1% TDS on transfers (from 1 Jul 2022), a de facto restrictive regime that drove most domestic volume offshore.
Finance Act 2022 imposed 30 percent tax on VDA gains and 1 percent TDS on transfers, a de facto restrictive regime pushing volume offshore.

actor: Banco Central de la Republica Argentina (BCRA)
one_line: BCRA Communication A 7506 prohibited financial institutions from offering or facilitating transactions in unauthorized crypto assets (a de facto ban since none are authorized), days after Banco Galicia enabled crypto buying.
BCRA Communication A 7506 barred financial institutions from offering unauthorized crypto transactions, a de facto ban.
Kazakhstan signed a 2022 law raising/restructuring the surcharge on electricity used by crypto miners (tiered by power price), tightening the mining regime ahead of the Feb 2023 Digital Assets Law.
BSP imposed a three-year moratorium (from Sept 1 2022) on accepting new VASP license applications, later extended indefinitely from Sept 1 2025 — closing market entry for new crypto exchanges.
Thai SEC banned digital-asset operators from offering deposit-taking, staking and lending ('depository') services with promised returns, following the 2022 crypto-lender collapses.

actor: US state securities regulators (CA, NY, KY, MD, OK, SC, WA, VT)
one_line: Eight US states filed coordinated enforcement actions against Nexo's Earn Interest Product as an unregistered security, with California's order announced as the eighth.

actor: US states CA NY KY MD OK SC WA VT
one_line: Eight US states filed coordinated enforcement actions against Nexo Earn Interest Product as unregistered securities.

actor: Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) / provincial regulators incl. OSC
one_line: CSA notice required all crypto trading platforms to sign a binding Pre-Registration Undertaking (no leverage, no unregistered stablecoins, custody segregation) or exit; triggered exits by OKX, Bybit, Paxos, dYdX, Bittrex, Deribit, and Blockchain.com (Binance covered separately).
CSA required crypto platforms to sign a binding Pre-Registration Undertaking or exit; triggered OKX, Bybit, Paxos, dYdX, Bittrex exits.

actor: Venezuela (SUNACRIP / national crypto regulator), Attorney General
one_line: Amid the PDVSA-Crypto corruption scandal, Venezuela suspended/reorganized SUNACRIP, arrested ~10 officials, and ordered crypto exchanges and mining farms to cease operations during the multi-month restructuring.
Venezuela suspended SUNACRIP amid a corruption scandal and ordered exchanges and mining farms to cease operations.

actor: Pakistan Senate Standing Committee on Finance / Ministry of Finance
one_line: Pakistan's Senate Finance Committee and Minister of State Aisha Ghaus Pasha stated crypto would 'never be legalized,' citing an FATF condition, signaling a permanent prohibition amid FIA notices to Binance's local representatives.

actor: Kuwait Capital Markets Authority + Central Bank of Kuwait + Insurance Regulatory Unit + Ministry of Commerce
one_line: Kuwait imposed an 'absolute prohibition' on virtual asset payments, investments, and mining (CMA Circular 10/2023, CBK circular, IRU Circular 6/2023, Ministerial Circular 1/2023), barring any local VASP licensing, citing FATF R.15.
Kuwait imposed an absolute prohibition on virtual-asset payments, investments and mining, barring local VASP licensing.

actor: Nigeria (EFCC, ONSA, SEC, NCC/telecoms, Central Bank of Nigeria)
one_line: Nigeria detained two Binance executives (Gambaryan, Anjarwalla), ordered telecoms to block access to Binance/Coinbase/other exchange sites, declared Binance unauthorized, and sought ~$10B penalty over alleged $26B untraceable flows; Binance delisted the naira.
Nigeria detained two Binance executives, ordered telecoms to block exchange sites, declared Binance unauthorized; Binance delisted the naira.

After the March 2024 NTC order to ISPs to block Binance's website, the SEC in April 2024 formally asked Apple and Google to remove the Binance app (and later Bitget/OKX/MEXC) from Philippine app stores for unregistered securities offering — the app-store/ISP enforcement layer distinct from the corpus's philippines-sec-binance-block-2024.

actor: Banco Central de Bolivia (with ASFI and UIF)
one_line: Bolivia's central bank lifted its 2014 crypto prohibition via Resolution No. 082/2024, authorizing financial institutions to process crypto transactions through approved electronic channels (a reversal/liberalization event, not a ban).
Bolivia lifted its 2014 crypto prohibition via Resolution 082/2024, authorizing banks to process crypto.

Kominfo, coordinating with Bappebti, blocked Instagram/social-media accounts and domains of unlicensed foreign exchanges (Binance, Bybit, Bitget, KuCoin, MEXC) for operating without Indonesian permits.

Virtual Asset User Protection Act came into force July 19 2024: prohibits market manipulation, use of material nonpublic information and unfair trading; FSC/FSS dedicated surveillance teams; first market-manipulation prosecution announced Nov 1 2024.

Following currency-defense pressure, the Central Bank of Iran restricted rial-to-crypto conversions on the Shaparak payment network and ordered a broad ban on deposits/withdrawals from crypto-exchange accounts (late Oct, reiterated late Dec 2024).
CBI restricted rial-to-crypto on Shaparak and banned deposits and withdrawals from crypto-exchange accounts to defend the rial.

Effective Jan 10-12 2025, regulatory and supervisory authority over crypto assets transferred from commodity regulator Bappebti to financial-services authority OJK (Govt Reg 49/2024 + OJK Reg 27/2024), reclassifying crypto as a digital financial asset with new licensing/AML obligations.

Payment processor Dwolla reversed ~$100K of credited transactions and blocked $70K of funds belonging to Bitcoin exchange TradeHill (reversing its 'no chargebacks' policy), forcing TradeHill to cease operations mid-Feb 2012; TradeHill sued Dwolla for ~$2M (filed Mar 5, 2012) — an early payment-rail de-risking of a Bitcoin exchange.

Capital One unilaterally closed the bank account of US Bitcoin exchange BitFloor, cutting off its USD deposit/withdrawal rail and forcing it to suspend operations in April 2013 amid the wave of FinCEN-guidance-driven de-banking of early Bitcoin exchanges.

After ~19,000 BTC (~$5M) stolen from operational hot wallets on Jan 4, Bitstamp froze user accounts, suspended trading, and blocked deposits/withdrawals for ~5 days (reopened Jan 9) while it rebuilt on new infrastructure.

actor: Cryptsy (US/Florida-based altcoin exchange; CEO Paul Vernon)
one_line: Cryptsy suspended trading and froze withdrawals in early Jan 2016, then announced insolvency claiming a 2014 hack of ~13,000 BTC; a Florida court receiver later alleged the CEO embezzled funds and fled, with users losing access to deposits.

After 119,756 BTC (~$72M) were stolen, Bitfinex halted trading, deposits and withdrawals (down 4-5 days) and imposed a socialized-loss 36% haircut across ALL customer balances, issuing BFX tokens as scrip compensation.
Bitfinex terminated trading/deposits/withdrawals for all US retail customers (effective by Nov 9 2017) and dropped US users from ERC-20/ICO tokens after SEC ICO-as-securities warning.
ShapeShift (CEO Erik Voorhees) announced mandatory KYC membership, ending anonymous no-account swaps; later cost ~95% of users — a foundational CEX privacy-censorship action.
Circle-owned Poloniex geofenced 9 tokens (ARDR, BCN, DCR, GAME, GAS, LSK, NXT, OMNI, REP) from US customers May 29 2019 over securities-classification uncertainty.
Binance.com updated terms to bar all US persons (effective Sept 12 2019 after 90-day grace), enforcing IP geofencing/redirects; launched separate Binance.US.
Binance DEX began IP geo-blocking the binance.org web interface for users from 29 countries including the US, Iran, Cuba, Syria, North Korea and Crimea — an early DEX frontend geofence.

GitHub restricted accounts of developers in Iran, Syria, Crimea, Cuba and North Korea (private repos, Marketplace, paid orgs) per US export-control/OFAC law, based on IP and payment geolocation — affecting many crypto-stack developers.
OKEx delisted five privacy coins in September 2019 to comply with FATF travel-rule guidance, part of the first major privacy-coin delisting wave (alongside Upbit).
Upbit ended support for six privacy coins (XMR, DASH, ZEC, XHV, TUBE, PIVX) effective Sept 30 2019, citing money-laundering concerns and FATF guidance.
Bittrex announced delisting of privacy coins Monero (XMR), Zcash (ZEC) and Dash (DASH); markets removed Jan 15, 2021 at 23:00 UTC, citing AML/KYC compliance.
Upbit (36 tokens incl. dark/privacy coins) and Bithumb delisted/flagged numerous coins ahead of mandatory FIU/FSC registration; many altcoins fell 50%+.
eToro announced delisting of Cardano (ADA) and Tron (TRX) for US customers by year-end 2021 (no new positions/staking after Dec 31) citing securities-regulatory concerns.

jurisdiction: Iran, Belarus, Cuba, DRC, Iraq, North Korea, Sudan, Syria, Zimbabwe, Crimea
one_line: PancakeSwap (leading BNB-chain DEX) implemented frontend geofencing blocking users from a list of OFAC-sanctioned jurisdictions including Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Syria and Crimea.

OpenSea deleted accounts of Iranian users and MetaMask/ConsenSys confirmed blocking users in OFAC-sanctioned jurisdictions (Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Syria, Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk) amid the Russia-Ukraine sanctions wave.

jurisdiction: Venezuela (collateral of US Donetsk/Luhansk sanctions config)
one_line: Infura misconfigured new US-sanctions geoblocks too broadly, cutting off MetaMask RPC service to Venezuelan users (and other regions) before apologizing and restoring access — an RPC-layer over-block incident distinct from the Donetsk/Luhansk block.
Binance froze crypto assets (~$21k BTC/ETH/USDT) of an account fundraising for Russian military supplies, after Ukrainian law-enforcement pressure.

Huobi Global announced delisting of seven privacy coins (XMR, ZEC, DASH, DCR, FIRO, XVG, ZEN); trading ended Sept 6, removal Sept 19 2022, citing regulatory pressure. (Corpus huobi entry is labeled 2024 — confirm date coverage.)
Magic Eden, the leading Solana/multichain NFT marketplace, restricts access from OFAC-sanctioned countries as a stated compliance measure, blocking sanctioned-jurisdiction users from its marketplace.

Apple refused to approve the Uniswap self-custody Wallet for the App Store, leaving it unavailable to iOS users despite approving comparable swapping wallets — an app-store gatekeeping block on a major DeFi frontend.
OKX informed Canadian users it would stop services and new accounts from Mar 24 2023 over new CSA regulations.

Orca, Solana's leading DEX, added the United States to its restricted regions and blocked US users from trading via orca.so (announced March 16, effective March 31, 2023), citing US regulatory uncertainty.

dYdX wound down access for Canadian users effective April 7, 2023, geofencing dydx.exchange from Canada (incl. Ontario) over the regulatory environment — distinct from its later US/Canada v4 geofence.
Paxos announced withdrawal from the Canadian market effective June 2 2023 amid CSA regulatory tightening.

Binance announced exit from Canada citing CSA stablecoin/investor-limit guidance making the market 'no longer tenable'; users to close positions by Sept 30 2023. (Corpus has the CSA-side S4 entry; this is the Binance corporate-exit mirror.)
Bybit announced it would cease serving Canadian users following the new CSA crypto-platform regulations.
Binance ceased all services for Netherlands users (effective July 17 2023) after failing to obtain Dutch VASP registration; urged migration to Coinmerce.
Binance withdrew from/abandoned multiple European markets in 2023 — deregistered in Cyprus, pulled Austrian and Belgian applications, withdrew German BaFin license bid — consolidating ahead of MiCA.
Gemini announced it would halt Netherlands operations by Nov 17 2023 due to DNB requirements on crypto exchanges.

jurisdiction: United States (DOJ seizure warrant; SDNY bankruptcy court)
one_line: Circle froze three Ethereum wallets holding ~$63M USDC tied to the $210M Multichain bridge hack at DOJ direction (Oct 2023); freeze later judicially extended for Multichain liquidators after the DOJ warrant lapsed.
Binance froze/seized 100+ accounts allegedly linked to Hamas fundraising at request of Israeli law enforcement in days after Oct 7 2023; ~200 more accounts placed on hold.

Apple briefly removed the MetaMask crypto wallet from the US App Store; it was restored within hours, prompting Coinbase's CEO to call for antitrust scrutiny of app-store gatekeeping over crypto apps.
Binance stopped accepting new UK users from Oct 16 2023 after FCA financial-promotions regime forced loss of its FCA-approver (Rebuildingsociety.com).
Binance froze ~220 Palestinian user accounts under an Israeli Anti-Terrorism-Law seizure order (Nov 2023 NBCTF letter), refusing appeals to restore funds; sparked controversy over over-broad seizure.

Bittrex Global announced winding down all platforms, with trading disabled from Dec 4 2023 (following US Bittrex bankruptcy/SEC settlement). The US-Bittrex SEC case is in corpus; the Global corporate shutdown is the distinct S5 offramp event.

Tether announced a voluntary policy to proactively freeze all wallets on the OFAC SDN list without awaiting law-enforcement request, immediately blocking 161 addresses (~3.5M USDT); a major shift from its 2022 stance of freezing only on instruction.

Binance announced global delisting of Monero (XMR) (alongside ANT, MULTI, VAI), trading halted Feb 20 2024 and withdrawals ended May 20; XMR fell ~30%. Distinct from the 2023 EU-jurisdiction privacy delisting already in corpus.

Binance discontinued all naira (NGN) services (P2P halted Feb 20, NGN deposits ended Mar 5, withdrawals ended Mar 8 2024), converting balances to USDT, amid Nigerian government clampdown and exec detentions.
OKX ceased Indian operations, asking users to withdraw by Apr 30 2024, after FIU-IND illegal-operation notices and Apple/Google app removals.
Tether, Binance and OKX assisted APAC law enforcement in freezing ~$46.9M USDT across five main wallets tied to a pig-butchering scam network (victims 2022-2023), traced via Chainalysis.
OKX discontinued all Nigeria services effective Aug 16 2024 (NGN/P2P removed May 2024), citing changes in local laws.

Tether, TRON and TRM Labs launched the T3 Financial Crime Unit, a private consortium executing USDT freezes via blacklisting at law-enforcement direction; it froze $100M+ by Jan 2025 and $450M+ by late 2025 across 20+ jurisdictions.
Coinbase delisted USDT, PAX, PYUSD, GUSD, GYEN and DAI for EEA retail users by Dec 13/30 2024 under MiCA non-compliant-stablecoin rules.
Bybit announced cessation of withdrawal/custody services for French users from Jan 8 2025 amid AMF regulatory pressure (later reversed Feb 2025 via Bybit EU).
Gate.io moved XMR, DASH, ZEC, ZEN, XVG perpetual contracts to reduce-only Dec 25 and fully delisted Dec 26 2024 amid MiCA privacy-coin pressure.
WazirX, with Tether's assistance, froze ~$3M USDT tied to its July 2024 $230M breach attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group.
Crypto.com announced suspension of USDT and 9 other non-MiCA-compliant tokens for European users by Jan 31 2025.
Tether froze 181,000 USDT linked to the $1.4B Bybit exploit attributed to the North Korea Lazarus Group; later assisted USSS in a related $9M freeze.
Binance announced delisting of nine non-MiCA-compliant stablecoins incl. USDT spot trading pairs for EEA users in March 2025 (derivatives retained).
Tether froze ~$27M USDT held by sanctioned Russian exchange Garantex following EU's 16th sanctions package, forcing Garantex to suspend all services and halt withdrawals.

Circle blacklisted 16 USDC addresses (exchanges, casinos, FX platforms) citing a sealed NY civil case; after ZachXBT criticism that the freeze was overbroad, Circle reversed several including a Goated.com wallet.
Tether and OKX froze ~$225.3M USDT across seven wallets at DOJ direction in the largest-ever pig-butchering civil forfeiture; Tether burned and reissued the tokens to the US government.

jurisdiction: United States (OFAC / Operation Economic Fury) vs Iran
one_line: Tether froze ~$344M USDT across two Tron addresses linked to Iran's IRGC/Central Bank under OFAC's Operation Economic Fury — its largest single on-chain freeze; later challenged by a lawsuit demanding return of funds.

actor: European Banking Authority (EBA), ESMA and EIOPA (Joint European Supervisory Authorities)
one_line: The three ESAs (EBA/ESMA/EIOPA) issued a joint consumer warning (Dec 13, 2013) on the high risks of buying/holding virtual currencies, noting they are unregulated under EU law and offer no legal protection — the earliest EU supranational action, predating the Jul 2014 EBA opinion already in corpus.

FATF October 2021 Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to VAs and VASPs — revised the 2019 guidance on stablecoins, P2P/unhosted wallets, VASP licensing and Travel Rule implementation. Distinct instrument from the 2021 targeted-update report in corpus.

FATF June 2022 Targeted Update on implementation of VA/VASP standards: only 29 of 98 surveyed jurisdictions had passed Travel Rule laws; flags DeFi, NFT and unhosted-wallet risks. Distinct from the 2021 and 2023 targeted updates already in corpus.

BCBS final standard on prudential treatment of cryptoasset exposures (SCO60, d545): two-group classification, 1250% risk weight and 1%-of-Tier-1 exposure cap for Group 2 cryptoassets; implementation 1 Jan 2025 (later moved to 2026). No Basel/BIS instrument currently in corpus.

FSB final High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Global Stablecoin Arrangements — distinct companion document to the FSB crypto-asset-activities framework already in corpus; sets GSC-specific reserve/redemption/governance expectations.

IMF-FSB Synthesis Paper 'Policies for Crypto-Assets', prepared for the Indian G20 Presidency — consolidates FSB regulatory recommendations with IMF macro-financial guidance into a unified policy/regulatory roadmap. Distinct from the G20 roadmap-endorsement entry in corpus.

IOSCO final report — 18 Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (CASPs), principles-based 'same activity, same risk, same regulation' covering conflicts of interest, market abuse, custody, cross-border. No IOSCO instrument in corpus.

IOSCO final report — 9 Policy Recommendations for Decentralized Finance (DeFi): addresses market integrity/investor protection, identifies 'responsible persons' behind DeFi arrangements for regulatory accountability.

FATF June/July 2024 Targeted Update on VA/VASP implementation: 65 of 94 jurisdictions had passed Travel Rule legislation; continued enforcement and supervision gaps. Not in corpus (corpus has 2021 and 2023 only).

BCBS final disclosure framework for banks' cryptoasset exposures (d580) plus targeted amendments to the cryptoasset standard (d579, incl. tighter stablecoin/Group 1b conditions); implementation 1 Jan 2026.

FSB report on the financial-stability implications of multifunction crypto-asset intermediaries / cross-border GSC use in emerging-market and developing economies (EMDEs) — warns of macro-financial risks from foreign-currency-pegged global stablecoins.
IOSCO final report on Investor Education on Crypto-Assets (FR06/2024): updated guidance for regulators designing retail investor-protection / warning initiatives on crypto risks.

G20 Crypto-asset Policy Implementation Roadmap — Status Report (22 Oct 2024): tracks progress on policy frameworks, capacity-building beyond G20, data gaps; commits FSB to a 2025 implementation review.

EU Transfer of Funds Regulation (recast, Reg 2023/1113) crypto Travel Rule becomes applicable to all EU CASPs — world's first zero-threshold implementation (originator/beneficiary data on every transfer incl. below EUR 1,000). Corpus has the 2023 adoption (eu-tfr-recast-2023) but not the Dec-2024 application milestone.

EU 16th Russia sanctions package — adds banks to the transaction ban for SPFS use to circumvent sanctions; continues the crypto/financial-messaging restriction track. Corpus stops at the 15th package (2024).

FATF June 2025 Plenary overhaul of Recommendation 16 (payment transparency / 'Travel Rule'): harmonizes data requirements across crypto and conventional cross-border payments, originator/beneficiary verification, USD/EUR 1,000 P2P threshold; compliance deadline end-2030.

FATF sixth Targeted Update (26 Jun 2025): 85 jurisdictions have Travel Rule legislation but only 29% largely compliant with R.15; urges stronger action on stablecoin illicit-finance risk (84% of illicit VA volume). New implementation table covering ~98% of global VASP activity.

EU 18th Russia sanctions package — lowers the threshold to impose a full transaction ban on third-country financial/credit institutions and crypto-asset service providers connected to Russia's SPFS; first non-Russian banks listed under the widened CASP/SPFS criteria.

IOSCO thematic review (FR/13/25) assessing implementation of its 2023 crypto/digital-asset-market recommendations across member jurisdictions; published alongside FSB joint note on progress toward comprehensive crypto regulation.

FSB Thematic Review of its 2023 global crypto-asset regulatory framework: finds significant gaps/inconsistencies; only 11 jurisdictions (EU, Japan, Singapore, HK, etc.) have finalised frameworks, flags data gaps and regulatory-arbitrage risk.

EU 19th Russia sanctions package — first EU prohibition on transacting a specific crypto-asset: bans the A7A5 rouble-backed stablecoin (Annex LIII, effective 25 Nov 2025), sanctions its developer/Kyrgyz issuer/trading platform, and bans provision of MiCA-defined crypto-asset services into Russia.

FATF Targeted Report on Stablecoins and Unhosted Wallets — Peer-to-Peer Transactions: recommends mitigations for stablecoin/unhosted-wallet illicit-finance risk; urges global P2P rules. Recent governance instrument absent from corpus.

FATF report 'Understanding and Mitigating the Risks of Offshore VASPs' — flags oVASPs used for scam/laundering, nested relationships; only 46% of jurisdictions use activity-based regulation. Calls for refusing business with unlicensed offshore providers.

EU 20th Russia sanctions package — categorical sectoral ban on all transactions with crypto-asset service providers and decentralized trading platforms established in Russia/Belarus (effective 24 May 2026); bans RUBx stablecoin and the digital rouble; same regime applied to Belarus.
